channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Russia, Ukraine and US meet for Abu Dhabi talks as Trump says war can 'end soon'
item.description: American, Ukrainian and Russian representatives gathered in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their latest round of trilateral peace talks.

item.title: Iran live updates: Trump says US will maintain 'status quo' with Tehran
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Fossil fuel emissions set to fall for first time since Covid, research shows
item.description: Global fossil fuel emissions are expected to fall by 0.4 percent in 2026 for first time since the Covid pandemic, driven by the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock linked to the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday, who warned the decline may be short-lived.

item.title: France threatens actions against Iran over supermarket cyberattacks
item.description: France will seek Europeans actions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage.

item.title: Hundreds more prisoners being released early
item.description: Hundreds more prisoners are being released early this morning, as part of a scheme to ease overcrowding in Britain's jails.

item.title: Teddy Riner announces candidacy for French presidential elections
item.description: Judo star Teddy Riner has announced his candidacy for the 2027 French presidential elections, against a backdrop of political tension across France.

item.title: Live: Ukraine, Russia and US resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States are meeting in Abu Dhabi for their first trilateral talks in more than nine months, as Washington pushes for an end to the war and Kyiv faces pressure to make territorial concessions. European representatives will also attend, amid fears that US President Donald Trump could press Ukraine to accept a deal on Moscow's terms. Follow our live blog for the latest developments.

item.title: Macrons file new defamation lawsuit against US podcaster over transgender rumours
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action.

item.title: Specialists to remove 25 lorry loads of waste from site a day
item.description: An operation has started to remove 18,000 tonnes of waste from an illegal site in Wigan.

item.title: California voters reject proposed one-time tax on billionaires' wealth
item.description: California voters have rejected a proposed 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires, handing a victory to tech leaders who poured hundreds of millions of dollars into defeating the measure. The defeat of Proposition 40 also marks a setback for progressives seeking to tax the wealth of the ultra-rich.

item.title: California voters defeat billionaire tax proposal that divided Democrats
item.description: The novel proposal would have charged billionaires a one-time 5% tax on most of their overall wealth, including their ownership in companies.

item.title: High air pollution alert issued as fog threatens travel disruption
item.description: Dense fog has led to a "high" air pollution alert being issued in London - as forecasters warn of difficult travel conditions and transport delays across much of the UK.

item.title: Amnesty urges El Salvador to disclose terms of Haiti troop deployment
item.description: Amnesty International has called on El Salvador and Haiti to make public the agreement governing the deployment of around 2,000 Salvadoran troops to the gang-plagued Caribbean nation, warning of risks to human rights and accountability.

item.title: FBI investigating Nvidia CEO over affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Donald Trump has said the FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy - but insisted he is a "very honourable man".

item.title: WATCH: 'Love is Blind' season 11, Erika Kirk: Here's what's trending
item.description: ABC's Rocsi Diaz takes a look at what's buzzing, including the Netflix series reunion not holding back and Erika Kirk speaking out after Dave Chappelle joked about her husband's assassination.

item.title: WATCH: What to expect from Bills-Vikings showdown
item.description: ESPN's Cameron Wolfe helps preview the matchup.

item.title: FDA orders blindness risk warning on weight loss drugs
item.description: Companies making popular weight loss drugs, including Ozempic and Wegovy, will be required to add a warning label about a rare eye condition that can cause blindness, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has said.

item.title: Nvidia shares slide as board probes CEO over affair with alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing scrutiny after reports he was targeted in a suspected Chinese intelligence operation involving a businesswoman with whom he was having an affair. The controversy has rattled investors, sending Nvidia shares tumbling.

item.title: US Defense Secretary Hegseth faces expected impeachment vote this week
item.description: A Republican lawmaker moved Monday to impeach US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting up a potentially explosive vote in Congress days after President Donald Trump's party suffered a crushing midterm defeat. Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment accusing Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorization and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

item.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on supermarket fridges
item.description: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot on Monday accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of being behind a recent cyberattack on French supermarket fridges, saying there would be consequences for the country.

item.title: France accuses Iran of cyber 'sabotage' in fridge attacks
item.description: France says Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 different retail sites last month, turning up temperatures in the middle of the night and spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food.

item.title: Nvidia: Honeypot may have been aimed at 'lobbying Jensen Huang to lobby the US government'
item.description: Nvidia ⁠and ​Chief ​Executive Jensen Huang were ​sued ‌on ⁠Monday ‌in ⁠a proposed class ​action accusing ‌them of ‌defrauding ​shareholders by concealing Huang's ties ​with ​a ​suspected ​Chinese spy. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Steve Tsang, Director of the SOAS China Institute, says that the affair "can also be about effectively lobbying Jensen Huang to lobby the US government, because he is a very powerful figure, particularly during the Trump administration, and he, for whatever reason, has been taking a position that is beneficial to Chinese development and advancement of its AI capacity".

item.title: Supreme Court lifts pause on border construction in Big Bend, Texas
item.description: The construction will include physical walls, access roads and vehicle barriers, according to Trump administration plans.

item.title: UK writer M. John Harrison wins Booker Prize for AI-tinged apocalyptic novel
item.description: UK author M. John Harrison won the Booker Prize on Monday for his enigmatic novel "The End of Everything", which echoes concerns about artificial intelligence in a darkly satirical depiction of post-apocalyptic Britain.

item.title: South Africa's ANC suffers historic setback in local elections as coalition talks begin
item.description: South Africa's ruling ANC suffers its worst-ever local election results, securing just 30 percent of the vote, as coalition talks loom. Meanwhile, former Ugandan military intelligence officer Herbert Matanda Mabonga accuses the army of secretly detaining and torturing opponents, following the release of videos that sparked national outrage. Finally, in Senegal, more than 200,000 free tickets are giving young people the chance to experience the Youth Olympic Games live on home soil, in a bid to inspire a new generation of athletes.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Supreme Court says border wall construction can continue in west Texas
item.description: The Trump administration filed an emergency relief request with the high court earlier in October asking for the construction to continue while a lawsuit over the plan moves forward.

item.title: What to expect as Russia, Ukraine and the US hold trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States are set to meet in the capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Tuesday for a new round of talks aimed at ending nearly five years of full-scale war triggered by Moscow's invasion of its neighbour. Security guarantees for the warring sides are set to top the agenda, with US officials insisting that a broader security architecture for Europe must be part of any peace deal.

item.title: WATCH: Inside the shadowy world of counterespionage
item.description: International Spy Museum's executive director Col. Chris Costa discusses the possible tactics the suspected Chinese spy used in the Nvidia scandal.

item.title: French Judo superstar Teddy Riner says will run for president
item.description: France's multiple Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday he would run in next year's presidential election, after expressing concern about the "rise of the far right". "My name is Teddy Riner and today, I am telling you face to face: I am a candidate in the 2027 presidential election," the 37-year-old said in a surprise announcement on social media. Riner, one of the greatest judokas in history, said in the two-minute-37-second video that he feared France could soon become deeply divided, appearing to cast himself as a candidate for voters unwilling to choose between two political extremes -- the far right and the hard left. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Yves Sintomer, Professor of Political Science at Université Paris VIII.

item.title: Thomas Massie files articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
item.description: The articles accuse Hegseth of "high crimes and misdemeanors," including for waging war against Iran in violation of the War Powers Resolution.

item.title: Trump says he was ‘kidding’ about Dana White press secretary job, amid online mix-up claims
item.description: Donald Trump says he was "only kidding" when he announced he had offered his friend and UFC boss Dana White the job of White House press secretary. The president shared an AI-generated video of White behind the briefing room podium and UFC fighters attacking journalists. But the announcement also sparked online speculation that Trump may have confused the UFC executive with a former Pentagon spokesperson, also called Dana White. There's no evidence of a mix-up, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: Nvidia's Huang scandal rattles AI industry built around him
item.description: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang sits at the center of the artificial intelligence boom, and the spy scandal that erupted over the weekend threatens to shake the company at a time when confidence in the AI investment frenzy is already fragile. Taiwan-born Huang is regarded as the godfather of the AI economy, the executive every player in the industry must turn to because the technology depends on the graphics processing units (GPUs) that his company designs. FRANCE 24's Wassim Cornet reports from Los Angeles.

item.title: Paris prosecutor opens probe into IRGC cyber unit Shahid Kaveh over fridge cyberattacks
item.description: The Paris prosecutor said she had opened an investigation into Shahid Kaveh, a shadowy cyber unit of the IRGC, the Islamic republic's ideological army, over the 'unprecedented' cyberattacks targeting French supermarkets' fridges in October. Little is known about the Shahid Kaveh unit, although analysts have long observed that the IRGC, which has a vast network of operations, had actively branched out into cyber warfare in recent years. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran.

item.title: 'Sexual predator' Russell Brand jailed for 10 years for rape, assault
item.description: British comedian and TV star Russell Brand was Monday jailed for more than 10 years for a string of sex offences including rape, as the judge told him he had been a "sexual predator" whose fame had protected him. Brand, 51, showed no emotion as judge Joel Bennathan said he had acted with "staggering arrogance" and shown "contempt" for his victims, who had suffered significant and lasting harm. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

item.title: Will Eisenkot succeed in 'minefield of Israeli politics' where 'so many other generals' have failed?
item.description: François Picard welcomes Dahlia Scheindlin, Israeli political analyst, strategic consultant and pollster, to examine a question that reaches far beyond the immediate struggle for power: Can Israel move beyond Netanyahu amid coalition deadlock, growing disillusionment in Washington and the persistent limits of political inclusion? As Gadi Eisenkot embarks on a 45-day race to form a government, following Israeli President Isaac Herzog's decision to entrust him with the task of assembling an elusive parliamentary majority, Scheindlin offers a timely reminder: “It's always too early to eulogize Netanyahu politically.” After all, the veteran prime minister has repeatedly demonstrated an extraordinary capacity to survive seemingly insurmountable political crises.

item.title: Republican congressman launches impeachment bid against Pentagon chief Hegseth
item.description: Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie moved on Monday to force a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, putting pressure on his fellow Republicans to decide whether to remove one of the Trump administration’s most prominent figures following the party's crushing defeat in midterm elections.

item.title: 'We think' the Iranians and Americans want to negotiate, Egyptian FM says
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said he believed Iran and the United States wanted to negotiate, but called for a "concrete deal" to prevent another escalation. He also said Cairo was still "counting" on US President Donald Trump to "move forward" with the stalled Gaza peace plan and was "confident" US military aid to Egypt would continue.

item.title: France opens probe into Iranian cyber unit over fridge attacks
item.description: France on Monday said Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind "unprecedented" cyberattacks on supermarket fridges in the country last month, vowing sanctions on a European level against Tehran. Swathes of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators, in some cases forcing them to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.

item.title: WATCH: Vikings' Aaron Jones shaped by military service
item.description: ABC News' Rebecca Jarvis reports ahead of the Vikings' Salute to Service game as running back Aaron Jones earns a nomination for the NFL's Salute to Service Award.

item.title: WATCH: New reaction to White House shake-up as newly elected Democrats head to Washington
item.description: President Donald Trump blamed bad messaging for the GOP's losses amid a White House shake-up that saw Stephen Miller, the architect of Trump's hard-line immigration policy, promoted to chief of staff.

item.title: WATCH: Disney launches 'Make the Holidays Magic' campaign
item.description: Disney kicks off the holiday season with a new short film called, “A Disney Holiday Short: The Invisible Horse.”

item.title: 'The South is in play': Longtime red states emerge as potential battleground for Dems
item.description: Democratic gains have encouraged some members of the party to point to the South as ground for increased investment ahead of the 2028 presidential cycle.

item.title: France blames Iran for massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges
item.description: France has accused Iran of being behind the massive cyber attack on supermarket fridges last month.

item.title: Jan. 6 should follow Trump 'to his grave,' Biden says in new memoir
item.description: Biden also said Trump "bordered on fawning" during 2024 Oval Office meeting

item.title: WATCH: Vikings superfan has only missed 2 home games in 25 seasons
item.description: “GMA” is outside U.S. Bank Stadium with Minnesota Vikings “Fan of the Year,” Lindsey Lorenston, as she is surprised with a pair of tickets to Super Bowl LXI.

item.title: Trump says he plans 'tremendous numbers' of pardons in 2nd half of term
item.description: The president also defended his pardons of Jan. 6 rioters.

item.title: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
item.description: New Delhi, home to over 30 million people, regularly ranks among the world's most polluted areas during winter, with pollution worsening in late October and November.

item.title: WATCH: Trump now showing 'great level of political acumen,' former staffer says
item.description: Harrison Fields served as the White House principal deputy press secretary from January to August 2025.

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand sentenced to over 10 years for rape and sexual assault
item.description: Russell Brand, who became a celebrity darling in the early 2000s, was found guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in a case brought by six women.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo XIV in Argentina
item.description: The pontiff will celebrate his first mass in Buenos Aires on Monday, which is expected to draw more than a million people.

item.title: James Bulger's mother 'relieved' as killer to remain in prison
item.description: James Bulger's mother has spoken of her overwhelming relief after the Parole Board said one of her son's killers should stay in prison.

item.title: WATCH: Family's gigantic fern named 'Jeff' goes viral on social media
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family in Colorado who has an annual tradition of having to move their gigantic fern, named Jeff, back inside for autumn.

item.title: Explosion at steel plant in Turkey kills 16, president says
item.description: A major fire broke out following an explosion at an iron and steel plant in Turkey on Monday killing 16 people, the country's president confirmed.

item.title: Why a South Korean city is turning to a U.S. college to outsmart AI?
item.description: Through civic participation and liberal education, South Korean educators hope to "quietly stitch the fabric of our democracy…before it unravels beyond repair."

item.title: Joe Biden scales back book tour as he reveals cancer treatment progress
item.description: Former US president Joe Biden said he won't be "able to have as many conversations" about his upcoming memoir as he would want to because of his cancer diagnosis.

item.title: Democrats won big on issues like immigration. But ICE still has the money
item.description: Following Tuesday's "blue wave," Democrats have vowed to reign in ICE's power. What could they actually accomplish?

item.title: On wild Cumberland Island, a land swap proposal stirs controversy
item.description: Visitors, ecologists, park rangers and residents all love this wild barrier island off the coast of southern Georgia. But they have different ideas of how to best protect it.

item.title: Trump says 'too tough' deportation policies hurt him in the midterms
item.description: "I think it was too tough," Trump said in an interview with CBS' "60 Minutes" that aired Sunday night. "And I think -- I think ultimately, that hurt me," he added.

item.title: At least 14 dead after boat carrying migrants found near Crete
item.description: At least 14 people have died after a boat carrying migrants was found near Crete, Greek authorities have said.

item.title: WATCH: NASA recruiting next generation of astronauts
item.description: NASA has released a new recruitment video, looking for new space explorers as it works to create a permanent base on the moon and someday possibly launching humans to Mars.

item.title: Georgia Gov.-elect Bottoms: 'It's safe to say that we are a blue state'
item.description: Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms joins "This Week" to discuss Democrats' sweeping victories, and her historic win in formerly red Georgia.

item.title: Seven dead and 114 injured in train crash near Cairo
item.description: At least seven people have died and more than 100 have been left injured in a major train crash south of Cairo, according to the Egyptian Chief Prosecutor’s office.

item.title: Finland's navy chief says Russia's presence in the Baltic Sea may have peaked for now
item.description: Russia may have reached the limit of its "peacetime" ability to project force in the Baltic Sea, with the maritime situation "tense" but "stable", the head of Finland's navy has said.

item.title: WATCH: Firefighters give kids a superhero surprise
item.description: Corpus Christi firefighters dressed as superheroes surprised patients at Driscoll Children's Hospital by rappelling down the glass building as kids waved.

item.title: Democrats flip statehouses in midterm wave
item.description: The showing across the country that flipped Congress to Democratic control on Election Day also trickled down to the state and local level.

item.title: Secret Service finds man parked near White House with multiple firearms: Authorities
item.description: The suspect, Ronny Guanipa-Chrinos, allegedly made threats to kill President Donald Trump, according to DHS.

item.title: WATCH: Guide dog Eddie named 2026 American Humane Society Hero Dog
item.description: Eddie, a 3-year-old Labrador retriever, was honored for changing the life of his legally blind owner, Luis Rodriguez, through his work as a guide dog.

item.title: WATCH: 1st look at Nat Geo's 'Wolves Up Close with Bertie Gregory'
item.description: The new National Geographic documentary follows Bertie Gregory to Canada's Hudson Bay as he captures rare wolf behaviors during the harsh Arctic winter.

item.title: Gunman suspected of killing six people in Polish city of Krakow has died, police say
item.description: A gunman suspected of killing six people including a British national in Poland on Saturday has died in hospital.
